spatial_claims.claim: ABCD is a parallelogram with diameter (diagonal) AC
O lies between A and C on diagonal AC
Line EG through O is parallel to AD, meeting AB at E and CD at G
Line HF through O is parallel to AB, meeting AD at H and BC at F
EG is parallel to BC (since AD parallel to BC)
HF is parallel to CD (since AB parallel to CD)
AEOH and OFCG are parallelograms about the diameter
Angle at A of AEOH equals angle at A of ABCD (shared vertex angle)
Angle at C of OFCG equals angle at C of ABCD (shared vertex angle)
Angle AEO equals angle ABC (by EO parallel to BC and transversal AB)
Angle OFC equals angle ABC (by OF parallel to AB and transversal BC)
Triangle AEO is equiangular with triangle ABC (shared angle at A, EO parallel to BC)
AE:EO = AB:BC (sides about equal angles at E and B, by 6.4)
AE = OH and EO = HA (opposite sides of parallelogram AEOH)
AB = CD and BC = DA (opposite sides of parallelogram ABCD)
Sides about every pair of corresponding equal angles in AEOH and ABCD are proportional
Triangle OFC is equiangular with triangle ABC (shared angle at C, OF parallel to AB)
OF:FC = AB:BC (sides about equal angles at F and B, by 6.4)
OF = CG and FC = GO (opposite sides of parallelogram OFCG)
Sides about every pair of corresponding equal angles in OFCG and ABCD are proportional
Both AEOH and OFCG similar to ABCD implies they are similar to each other (by 6.21)

configuration_map: ABCD is a parallelogram with diagonal AC. Point O lies on segment AC between A and C. Through O, line EG is drawn parallel to sides AD and BC, meeting AB at E and CD at G. Through O, line HF is drawn parallel to sides AB and CD, meeting AD at H and BC at F. This creates two sub-parallelograms about the diagonal: AEOH (at the A-corner, with vertices A on corner, E on AB, O on diagonal, H on AD) and OFCG (at the C-corner, with vertices O on diagonal, F on BC, C on corner, G on CD). In triangle ABC, segment EO connects point E on AB to point O on AC and is parallel to BC, making triangle AEO similar to triangle ABC. In triangle ABC, segment OF connects point O on AC to point F on BC and is parallel to AB, making triangle OFC similar to triangle ABC. All points maintain consistent positions throughout the proof.
pass_reason: All spatial claims are mutually consistent. The construction is standard: a point O on diagonal AC of parallelogram ABCD with parallel lines through O creating sub-parallelograms. The triangle similarities (AEO ~ ABC via EO parallel to BC; OFC ~ ABC via OF parallel to AB) are geometrically valid, and the proportionality chains derived from these similarities combined with parallelogram opposite-side equalities all check out correctly. No angle decomposition issues arise since the proof uses direct triangle similarity (6.4) rather than angle sums, and no point position contradictions exist.
